tier_reason: README Benchmarks section embeds test/benchmark/results/avg-ops-per-sec.svg whose text carries exactly markdown-wasm 195,065, markdown-it 84,774, marked 76,942, commonmark 66,185, showdown 8,502 ops/s (and avg-throughput.svg 49 vs 17 MB/s); the harness test/benchmark/bench.js is public, but the machine is only a '2.9 GHz MacBook' (no CPU model) and the emcc version and optimisation level are not stated, so first-party tier C.

corrections.baseline: markdown-it ^10.0.0 (commonmark preset, IDNA link encoding disabled), marked ^0.7.0, commonmark.js ^0.29.2 and showdown ^1.9.1 (JavaScript) in Node.js 14.11 / V8
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Built with wasmc ^2.2.1 (an emcc wrapper); wasmc.js release cflags are only -DMD4C_USE_UTF8, so the optimisation level is wasmc's default; emcc/wasmc versions used for the run not stated
corrections.claimed_speedup: Average ops/second from the README chart test/benchmark/results/avg-ops-per-sec.svg: markdown-wasm 195,065; markdown-it 84,774; marked 76,942; commonmark 66,185; showdown 8,502 (2.3x over markdown-it, derived from page data). Average throughput chart: 49 MB/s vs 17 MB/s for markdown-it (2.9x, derived from page data). A later third-party run in ije/md4w (Apple M1, Deno 1.40.5, commonmark-spec.md) shows markdown-wasm 2.16 ms/iter vs markdown-it 14.0.0 5.19 ms/iter (2.4x, derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: Author's own 2020-era run (Node 14.11) on a '2.9 GHz MacBook' with no CPU model; emcc version and optimisation level not stated, hence tier C. The README values appear only in SVG charts; results/bench.csv is not committed (404). Harness asymmetry: bench.js feeds markdown-wasm a UTF-8 Buffer and calls parse(..., {asMemoryView:true}), so it skips string encoding of input and string decoding of output, while every JS library takes and returns JS strings; the README itself says the bytes/memory-view mode only helps when output is never converted to a string. The averaged ops/s is an unweighted mean across sample files, and the JS baselines are old versions (markdown-it 10, marked 0.7). A later third-party run (ije/md4w test/benchmark.js, string output, markdown-it 14.0.0) still shows about 2.4x, so the direction holds. md4w reports itself about 1.14x faster than markdown-wasm. Repository unmaintained since July 2021.

notes: Numbers verified in the SVG chart text; tier stays C (no CPU model, no emcc version). Shortcomings: benchmark gives markdown-wasm a bytes-in/memory-view-out fast path the JS baselines do not get, stale baseline versions, abandoned since 2021-07-06; md4w's independent Deno run corroborates about 2.4x over markdown-it 14.0.0.

tier_reason: Upgraded C to A: benchmark code is public (test/benchmark.js, deno bench, markdown-it@14.0.0 and markdown-wasm-es@1.2.1 pinned), the compiler is stated (README Development section names Zig 0.11.0, present at the screenshot commit a2ff722 of 2024-02-21), flags are in build.zig (ReleaseFast for md4w-fast.wasm, which index.js loads from the file system as the bench does; build.zig unchanged since that commit), and the screenshot names the CPU (Apple M1) and runtime (Deno 1.40.5).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Zig 0.11.0 (README Development section, also at the screenshot commit a2ff722), build.zig optimize mode ReleaseFast for md4w-fast.wasm (loaded from the file system, which test/benchmark.js does) with md4c.c compiled with no extra C flags; ReleaseSmall for md4w-small.wasm; run with Deno 1.40.5
corrections.claimed_speedup: README: about 2.5x faster than markdown-it. Screenshot test/benchmark-screenshot.png: md4w 1.89 ms/iter (529.1 iter/s), markdown-wasm 2.16 ms/iter (462.0 iter/s), markdown-it 5.19 ms/iter (192.6 iter/s); 5.19/1.89 is 2.7x over markdown-it and 2.16/1.89 is 1.14x over markdown-wasm (derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: Results are a terminal screenshot (no text table) from a single input file (test/commonmark-spec.md), single machine, one run, last updated 2024-02-21; vendored md4c was updated afterwards (2024-03-15) without a new run. The Zig version comes from the README's Development note rather than the run itself. The wasm libraries get the input as a Uint8Array while markdown-it gets a pre-decoded string (small advantage to the wasm side); markdown-it runs its default preset (html off, linkify off) while md4c runs its own default flags, so outputs are not checked for equality. markdown-wasm is measured through markdown-wasm-es@1.2.1, an ES-module repackaging published by md4w's author. Win over markdown-wasm (same md4c core) is only 1.14x. Author's own benchmark.

notes: Numbers match the screenshot exactly; upgraded to A because Zig 0.11.0, ReleaseFast (build.zig), Apple M1 and Deno 1.40.5 are all stated and the harness is public. Shortcomings: single-file screenshot run from Feb 2024, input-type asymmetry, no output-equality check, only 1.14x over markdown-wasm; stale (last commit 2025-05-28).

tier_reason: doc/project/webassembly.md states 'geomean 30% lower run time across our benchmarks' versus the JS output, and the 1.19.0 announcement states 15% lower; both are first-party sentences with no benchmark list, engine, hardware or harness named, so tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Scala.js WebAssembly backend documentation: for applications dominated by computation inside Scala code the Wasm output should be significantly faster than the JS output (geomean 30% lower run time across our benchmarks, about 1.43x, derived from page data). The 1.19.0 announcement (2025-04-21) gave geomean 15% lower running time. Interop-heavy code may be significantly slower; generated code size about twice as large in fullLink mode.
corrections.caveats: The 30% geomean figure (and the earlier 15% in the 1.19.0 release post) is a first-party sentence with no benchmark list, machine, engine version or harness named; the release post adds that the benchmarks do not measure JS interop in any significant way. The likely suite (scalajs-benchmarks: richards, deltablue, tracer, sha512, json and others, BSD-3-Clause) publishes no results. Third-party recaps (VirtusLab blog: up to 3.3x over JS on Marr et al.'s cross-language suite, snippet only; ICFP/SPLASH 2025 Wasm workshop abstract) could not be opened, and VirtusLab co-develops the backend. Baseline is Scala.js's own JS backend, not hand-written JavaScript or TypeScript. No @JSExport support and single-module output only.

notes: Quote verified on the raw doc page; tier C holds (first-party, no methodology). Shortcomings: unspecified benchmarks/engine/hardware, figure moved from 15% (1.19.0) to 30% (docs) with no data, interop-heavy code slower, 2x code size; repo active (last commit 2026-10-11), Apache-2.0, 4.7k stars.
